rows.interpretation: The Royal Mint dates the overlap from 28 March 2017, when the new pound became legal tender, to 23:59 on 15 October 2017, when the round pound lost that status. The Mint's chief executive expected to melt down many returned round pounds and reuse their metal to strike new coins. The July 10 announcement's one billion is the number of new pounds produced. The number of round pounds returned is missing.
rows.uncertainty: The dates and intended reuse are explicit, but the July production figure cannot establish the number returned.
rows.unanswered: How many old round pounds had been returned by the July update?
